mainEntity.name: What is the difference between drain cleaning and drain clearing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clearing deals with a drain that is blocked right now. Cleaning is planned work on a line that is still flowing, done to stop it reaching that point. If your drain is blocked today, the page you want is blocked drains. If it has blocked before and you would rather it did not again, this is the right page.

mainEntity.name: How often should drains be cleaned?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on what goes through the line and what the camera found last time, which is why the first visit always includes a look rather than just a clean. Commercial kitchens are usually the shortest interval because of the volume of fat involved. A home with no history of blockages generally does not need a schedule at all, and we will say so.

mainEntity.name: Does cleaning stop tree roots coming back?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Cleaning removes what has grown in, but the roots return to the same opening because that is where the moisture is. The interval buys you time rather than solving it. Sealing the pipe is what stops it. Relining closes the joints and cracks the roots are entering through, and after that the line generally does not need a schedule.

mainEntity.name: Can you clean drains in an occupied building?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Most scheduled work is done in occupied homes, unit blocks and trading premises. Access is through existing openings and the disruption is limited to the area around them. For commercial kitchens the visit is usually booked outside service hours so the line is not in use while it is being cleaned.
